hook: Jane Austen's First Novel Was Rejected Unread
text: In November of seventeen ninety-seven, a country clergyman wrote to a London publisher. He said he had a novel in three volumes, written by someone in his family, and asked if it might be published. The answer came back by return of post. No, thank you. The publisher never even asked to see it. The novel was called First Impressions. It was written by his twenty-one-year-old daughter, Jane. Sixteen years later, revised and renamed, it was published as Pride and Prejudice. And readers have loved it ever since.
